title: Authentic Swahili Mahamri
author: Chef Amina Hassan

relatedDish.note: KEN101 is a category entry for Mahamri in the Breads & Breakfast section. The primary recipe with full heritage, cultural notes, and detailed technique is KEN016 (Authentic Swahili Mahamri). Both describe the same dish.

desc: Mahamri — the Swahili coast's most celebrated fried bread — light, yeast-leavened, fragrant with coconut milk and cardamom, and deeply satisfying. The defining breakfast of coastal Kenya. See KEN016 for the full recipe and heritage.
longDesc: Mahamri uses yeast rather than baking powder, giving it a lighter, airier texture and a richer coconut flavour than Mandazi. The dough needs 90 minutes to proof — the patience is rewarded with breads that puff magnificently in the oil. Along Kenya's coast, the smell of mahamri frying before morning prayer during Ramadan is one of the most evocative aromas in Swahili food culture.
steps: Combine flour, sugar, yeast, cardamom, and salt. Mix well.
Add lukewarm coconut milk, egg if using, and oil. Mix into a soft dough.
Add warm water gradually until dough comes together.
Knead for 8—10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Place in oiled bowl, cover, and proof in a warm place for 1½ hours until doubled.
Punch down gently. Divide and roll to 1cm thick.
Heat oil to 170°C. Fry in batches for 2—3 minutes per side until golden and puffed.
Drain on paper towels. Serve warm.
chefTips: Coconut milk must be lukewarm — hot liquid kills the yeast.
Full 90-minute proof is essential for the airy texture.
Freshly ground cardamom from whole pods is dramatically more fragrant.
commonMistakes: Too-hot coconut milk — kills the yeast.
storage: Store in airtight container for 3 days. Freeze for 2 months.
reheating: Warm in oven at 160°C for 5 minutes.
culturalNote: Mahamri is the fried bread of Swahili coastal celebrations — prepared for Ramadan, Eid, and family gatherings across Mombasa, Lamu, and Malindi.
